spec_issues: The overview and the prompt agree. The prompt states the bars (99% overall, 98.5% per noise group), the 5 s per-search cap, the 0.9 s average per-tree shard budget, that private trees are fresh, and says 'so keep a margin'. Practice-tree generation is explicitly allowed (eval_harness/utils/trees.py). No hidden rule decided any outcome.
The validity rule is a hard cliff: one tree below 99.0% overall turns a reward of about 1.5 into 0. 'Keep a margin' is the only guidance; nothing says how large.

The disqualification process is undisclosed, but nothing in this task needed it. The 3 valid=0 trials (Grok nU5YYUV, Grok w95Swje, Argon ahhVHDn) have no stated reason. Both Astra trials have an empty reward breakdown (rewards={}), so their private accuracy and validity cannot be checked. Kimi T6xcqyV scored despite exception=AgentContinuationStalledError.
verifier_issues: What makes a submission invalid (eval_harness/utils/evaluation.py): valid = candidate_accuracy >= 0.99 overall AND every bin >= 0.985 (report['valid'] = int(report['candidate_accuracy_ok'])), or any crash, timeout over 5 s, protocol error, or total shard time above 0.9 s x cases (which includes tree generation and the baseline search). Cost = geometric mean over the 4 bins of mean revealed nodes; reward = baseline/candidate - 1.

The public verifier uses a fixed tree set (score_config.json master_seed 2026, 2000 trees per bin = 8,000 trees). The private set is 16,000 fresh trees, 4,000 per bin. Because the public trees are fixed and reproducible offline (make_cases(2026, ...) / tree_seeds(2026, ...)), an agent can select changes that add zero errors on exactly those 8,000 trees. That inflates public accuracy relative to fresh trees. Grok w95Swje called tree_seeds(2026, ...) 1,244 times and Argon ahhVHDn called make_cases(2026, ...) 462 times. Fable and Astra validated on independent seeds.

The node-count objective is stable. Fable 5gC2NsY measured 417.1-419.5 nodes on four independent 20k-tree-per-bin runs, 419.9 on public and 421.0 on private. Fable WFDwh5f: 655.4 public, 656.9 private. Astra: public reward 1.654/1.877 vs private 1.649/1.885. The private baseline objective is fixed (1297.02) for every trial, so there is no baseline-re-measurement noise.

The 3 invalid trials look correctly invalid on accuracy grounds. Grok w95Swje's final file passed public by one tree (99.01% overall; bins 99.30/99.00/98.95/98.80). Argon ahhVHDn's own fresh 8,000-tree check 'CD-8000' showed 98.975-98.987% overall, below the bar, and it shipped anyway. Grok nU5YYUV reached 99.28%/99.15% minimum bin on public only after 1,517 public evaluations and explicit selection for 'zero additional errors on the public set'. Its fresh-tree accuracy was very likely lower. Timing is not the cause for any of them: max per-tree times are 0.22-0.36 s.
task_level.noise: Node counts are low-noise (an estimated reward SE of about 0.02-0.03 from 4,000 trees per bin; observed public-to-private shifts of 0.01 or less in reward for validated runs). Validity is the noisy part. Several scored runs sat close to the cliff on public: Argon 3J9vt7s 99.21% overall / 99.00% minimum bin, Kimi T6xcqyV 99.22% / 98.75%, Flash xzuJjnb 98.90% minimum bin, Astra HYcHHWh 99.00% minimum bin. They passed private, while the invalid Grok nU5YYUV had better public margins (99.28% / 99.15%). With the private overall SE near 0.08 percentage points, pass or fail for a run whose true accuracy is about 99.0-99.1% is close to a coin flip, so validity of near-cliff runs is partly luck. The large gap between Fable's two attempts (2.08 vs 0.97) is not grader noise: each run's score is reproducible within about 1% across independent seeds. It reflects two different algorithms (a decision search with soft claims plus explicit error-probability verification, vs Bayesian-guided alpha-beta with a more conservative risk budget, 99.70% public accuracy). In Elo terms the noise sits in agent-run variance, not measurement.
task_level.epoch_rationale: The winner, Fable 5gC2NsY (2.08), was validated on independent seeds and is stable to within 1%. The invalid runs are correctly invalid under the stated accuracy bars, and the validity-cliff luck affects only lower-placed runs, so no scoring defect changes the task winner.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: Mostly genuine science. The top 4 scores (Fable 5gC2NsY 2.08, Astra 1.88/1.65, Argon 3J9vt7s 1.62) come from substantive algorithmic ideas. All exploit that leaves are exact and noise is structured: interval bounds propagated from exact leaves, Bayesian or Kalman models of walk level plus correlated heavy-tailed noise, null-window proofs, and risk budgets on the root decision (Fable). Astra adds learned calibrated cut predictors trained offline on fresh generated trees. These are known families (probabilistic or Bayesian game-tree search, ProbCut-style forward pruning, learned pruning) but well executed. The gaming is confined to the 3 invalid runs, which tuned to the fixed public tree set and the public bar (Grok w95Swje: 'the current file sits exactly one tree' above the bar). The verifier's fresh private trees correctly punished all 3. Mid-pack runs (Flash, Kimi) are routine margin and PVS tuning of the starter.

trials.approach: Rewrote the search as a risk-bounded decision search. Exact [lo, hi] bounds are propagated from leaf values, and decision-oriented null-window tests run on root children. Frontier nodes can be 'soft-claimed' by posterior quantiles from a structural prior: walk level inferred by Gaussian belief propagation, parent-child AR(1) noise with a per-tree rho posterior, and ML estimation of a Gaussian/t6/t3 noise-scale mixture. Search continues until the estimated probability of a wrong root decision is under a per-tree budget.

trials.approach: Bayesian-guided alpha-beta. Each expanded node's children get a group model (walk location, minimax-deviation mixture, shared plus heavy-tailed noise) evaluated on a numeric grid. A node is cut when the posterior probability that the cut is wrong falls below a relevance-allocated tolerance. The root gets a one-sided proof for the leader and null-window refutations for the rest. Calibrated conservatively: 99.70% public accuracy.

Final summary: 'Fresh-seed validation (10 seeds x 16 000 trees ...): overall accuracy 99.57% (min 99.51%), per-bin minimum 99.42%, mean objective ~654'; public 655.4, private 656.9

trials.approach: PVS with depth-2 root lookahead ordering, a pooled sibling-variance noise estimate, and depth-indexed forward-pruning margins interpolated between low-noise and high-noise tables, including pre-expansion beta cuts. Standard search engineering on the starter.

trials.approach: 'Kalman-smoothed zero-window separation search'. Top-down and bottom-up Gaussian messages estimate each node's true value from the walk prior, siblings and exact leaves. Zero-window probes separate the top two root candidates using confidence multipliers (C_BASE 2.55, C_POST 2.60) and depth tables of advantage and minimax offsets fitted offline. Tuned on a mix of the public seed and fresh seeds (9999, 55555, 77777, ...).

trials.approach: Cached threshold proofs over exact minimax intervals, plus cost-aware best-first work. Learned, conservatively thresholded cut predictors (several .npz models trained offline on hundreds of thousands of freshly generated query and root samples) close confident threshold queries under a work-proportional risk budget. Contradictions or a work cap fall back to exact search.

trials.approach: PVS with multi-evidence cut tests: prune only when the node's own observation and its best child's observation (and, for fail-high, the parent bound) all agree at moderate z. Margins are scaled by online per-depth noise from exact residuals, terminal fraction and child rank. Tuned on practice seeds (777 and per-bin seeds).
